chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: Hearing the Six Spirits of Rhythm and first smoking pot
summary: Collins first heard the Six Spirits of Rhythm playing high at a pad and started smoking pot as an escape while his mother was ill and he waited tables.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Like when you said everybody at the Royal Roost was a junkie.
Well, Miles was at one point.

Well, I think Miles is now. But I mean, I think at that time Miles drank beer. I don't think he even smoked cigarettes at this time. But this was after the war, when I came out, you know, maybe it had something to do with the War hysteria, worst area, of conditions during the war, I don't know. Because I was in the army so I wouldn't know what was happening out in that area, you know, outside in that area. But I know that when I started smoking pot [my] -- I tell you, I went to pad

and I heard the six spirits of rhythm. Now, this Pad -- I had never smoked any pot, but I was an admirer of the six spirits of rhythm, you know, the -- Leo Watson and all of them. So there was a pad across the street from where I lived, the guy's name was Speedy, and I had never been in Speedy's place in my life but I knew -- someone told me that the six spirits of rhythm would go in every day and play and they'd get high, so I wanted to hear them play.

And I went over there and they were smoking pot, and getting high and playing and they would really play, you know. So I said, well geez, it can't be too bad if they can play. Now here we go, okay. If they can play and perform like that, it can't be too bad. I didn't smoke any then, but later I did. So it was a ball, you know, I laughed a lot and all of this, and I smoked it during that -- another reason I smoked it during that time, because my mother was ill, she was very ill, and we financially were in pretty bad straits, you know. And I had to work. And I couldn't associate with the musicians that I -- because I had to get out and get a job. I think at this time I was washing dishes or doing something, I don't know, waiting tables, which I've done all of that, during this time.
And for me it was an escape. I wouldn't -- things weren't quite as bad, you know, I could kind of bear up under it. But -- and so I smoked, and then when I -- I used to

sneak and smoke and my mother was aware that I was smoking. But after a while she was, but she never said anything to me about it, you know, but I knew that she knew. Well, I never did smoke in front of her.
